title: Advanced Reinforcement Learning Algorithms to Optimize Design Verification
problem: Achieving comprehensive coverage of hard-to-hit states in hardware design verification is challenging as integrated circuit complexity increases. Existing verification methods struggle to efficiently generate optimal stimulus settings to maximize coverage in complex architectures like MESI cache controllers.
motivation: Machine learning-based automation of design verification can significantly improve coverage detection and reduce verification effort for complex hardware designs.
method: The paper uses Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), a machine learning algorithm that learns what test inputs work best for exposing chip behaviors, enhanced with Prioritized Experience Replay to focus more on the most informative past test runs. The goal is to maximize the average FIFO queue depth—a measure of how fully the data buffer is used—in a MESI cache controller managing four CPUs. Results are compared against DDPG with uniform experience replay and Bayesian Optimization.
key_novelty: Combining prioritized experience replay with DDPG to automatically generate hardware verification tests that find rare, hard-to-reach states in complex chip designs.
contributions: DDPG-PER framework for automated stimulus generation in hardware design verification
Empirical demonstration that prioritized experience replay improves DDPG effectiveness for verification coverage
Increased FIFO depth and coverage on MESI cache controller compared to baselines
Significantly faster convergence than Bayesian Optimization with reduced execution time

metrics.other: average FIFO depth, coverage improvement, execution time reduction

primary_theme: Machine learning for automated hardware design verification
